issue.title: Extract SocketAdress logic from NameResolver

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:

As discussed in #4529, NameResolver design shouldn't be resolving SocketAddresses (or String name + port) and return InetSocketAddresses. It should resolve String names and return InetAddresses.
This SocketAddress to InetSocketAddresses resolution is actually a different concern, used by Bootstrap.   

Modifications:

Extract SocketAddress to InetSocketAddresses resolution concern to a new class hierarchy named `AddressResolver`.
These `AddressResolver`s delegate to `NameResolver`s.

Result:

Better separation of concerns.

Note that new `AddressResolver`s generate a bit more allocations because of the intermediate `Promise` and `List<InetAddress>`.

body:
@normanmaurer Sorry, I don't follow.

Here's how I've been doing things prior to 4.1:
- Channel initially have a HttpClientCodec
- Send initial upgrade request
- If status is different from 101, perform standard HTTP operations such as redirect or auth, and perform upgrade request again
- Otherwise, add the WebSocketEncoder and Decoder in the pipeline, based on HttpClientCodec position, and remove HttpClientCodec. HttpClientCodec lookup is based on the name that was used to set it in the first place.

But now with 4.1:
- HttpClient is no longer a Handler in the pipeline. There's an Encoder and a Decoder instead, whose names are not even based to the name that was used to set the HttpClientCodec.
- I had to use the internal names for the Encoder and Decoder (`HttpClientCodec$Decoder#0` and such) to remove them and find out where to place the WebSocket handlers.

[Definitively hacky. Maybe/probably I'm doing it wrong.](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/blob/netty4.1/client/src/main/java/org/asynchttpclient/netty/channel/ChannelManager.java#L451-L461)
But I think the new design overlooked the fact that the WebSocket handler didn't cover the fact that the handshake response could be something else than 101 and be perfectly valid and have to be handled downstream.
@slandelle so the real problem is more or less that HttpClientCodec is not working as before in the terms that it just "stays" in the pipeline ?
@slandelle gotcha... I think this is more or less a breaking change so I'm wondering if we should just make it work as before. Does this sound good ?
That would be awesome and make upgrading a bliss!
@trustin WDYT ? I can take care of this

@trustin @Scottmitch @slandelle another thing we could do is change the `HttpClientCodec` and others to basically still keep itself in the pipeline and remove the encoder/decoder once itself was removed. That said I think maybe we should just remove `ChannelHandlerAppender` and undeprecate `ChannelDuplexHandler`. It just sounds like this one will give the user less surprises as the handler that they add to the pipeline will just stay there and they can remove it as usual. 

I think this is something we need to fix before 4.1.0.Final
